reviews.text:
I left this clinic heartbroken after losing my pet rat, and deeply upset by the cost of the visit: nearly $600.

The vet attempted to relieve a urinary blockage with a catheter but was unsuccessful. Surgery was quoted at around $800, with no guarantee of success, and my rat was ultimately euthanized.

The estimate included $115 for the examination, $81.90 for anesthesia and monitoring, $18.76 for pain medication, $62.08 for professional services, $153.74 for euthanasia, and another $106 for communal cremation without the return of his ashes, plus tax.

I understand that veterinary work costs money, even when treatment is unsuccessful. My complaint is about how expensive the entire visit was, including the separate charges for euthanasia and communal cremation.

Losing a beloved pet is devastating. Leaving with a bill of nearly $600 made an already terrible day even harder. In my opinion, these prices are excessive.

- Update following the owner’s response:

My review concerns the cost of the visit. I acknowledged that your team attempted treatment and that veterinary work must be paid for, even when it is unsuccessful.

Telling me not to “take my sorrow out” on your team dismisses my concern rather than addressing it. Suggesting that reviews like mine are why clinics refuse to treat small animals is unfair to a grieving owner.

You are entitled to explain your fees, and I am entitled to describe my experience and express my opinion about the cost. I would have appreciated a respectful explanation rather than blame.
Had pet rats neutered here and they are doing very well now!

I was a little worried before coming because I noticed the clinic only had a 4.1-star rating. But after my visit, I realized ratings are relative, and my experience was genuinely excellent.

I brought my Russian tortoise in for a beak trim today. The veterinarian was incredibly patient and gentle—not only with my tortoise, but also with me, taking the time to explain everything and making sure we both felt comfortable.

The procedure was completed quickly and professionally, and the total cost was under $70, which I thought was very reasonable.

I'm very happy with the experience and wouldn't hesitate to bring my tortoise back here in the future. Thank you for taking such good care of exotic pets!

Dr. Sydnie Jones was patient and took the extra time to warm up to our two nervous German Shepherds before getting hands on for their exams and shots. This empathic and caring approach was much appreciated vs the ‘straight to the muzzle’ approach.

They are very gentle with my guinea pigs .
The black one is Coolio and the other one is Limp Bizkit

Uri is not even a proper human let alone a vet. Extremely arrogant and lack of proper knowledge. Rough handling, and no compassion at all.

DO NOT GO TO THIS VET.

I was impressed with the staff and their knowledge of hamsters. Most of the time when I go to a vet I know more about hamsters than they do, but that was not the case here.

The only reason i’m not giving 5 stars is because the pricing is insanely expensive.

I’ve been to other vets in different cities for hamsters before and their prices were much more reasonable.

I was a bit taken aback by how many checkups they wanted to do considering the cost and the fact that i’m 99% sure we would have just continued with the same treatment plan.

It seemed like tests and fees just kept piling up and I didn’t feel confident that they were making sure to do things in the most cost effective way.

I know I know…all the vets are being bought up and monopolized and slowly raising prices everywhere. I guess i’m hoping that a google review, the only option we have left to voice concerns, will actually make a difference.

The staff are extremely skilled and knowledgeable. The low review is more aimed at the predatory system every clinic is apparently being forced to become a part of.
Proffessiional Service and Friendly!
Dope staff! Everyone is very thoughtful and caring! Our cats love Dr. Uri! Would alway recommend this place to any pet owner!

Having taken more than one of my pets here for a few visits, the experience has always been consistently welcoming and the care for both my geckos has been impressive. The reptile expertise at this clinic is obvious and the care level reflects that.

This review is regarding Dr. Burstyn's informative videos.

I recently recommended Dr. Burstyn's YouTube channel to someone who had learned that their cat had both hyperthyroidism and CKD and that person felt quite lost. I recommended this channel and I realized that its content had helped me a lot when I was the one feeling lost when my cat had a uremic crisis. At that time, I didn't know a lot about CKD and I was so overwhelmed by everything. I went back home with my cat on the back seat of the car, I stopped at a red light, melted in tears and told her that I didn't want her to die. I didn't wanna hospitalize her because the costs seemed too high for me so I arrived home with fluids at 10 PM with no one to help me administer them. I was shaking, it was chaotic and my cat didn't like me too much at that moment. But you know what? She got better. Then I've watched a lot of Dr. Burstyn's videos and listened carefully to his explanations. In addition, watching them helped me feel better about all that. The way he explains things with such calm and a smile, it's a balm for the soul. Seriously. At least it's been for me.

So almost two years later, at 17, my cat is doing pretty good and I really thank him for that. Sure, I have very helpful vets and I'm super grateful to them. But when you're at home at night, anxious, wondering what to do and what's gonna happen, you watch the Helpful Vancouver Vet and it helps 🙂
Uri Burstyn is condescending and insensitive.

I don't usually leave reviews but felt like I had to with this one. They told me about the laparoscopic spay option after I'd already been quoted for the regular one, but I couldn't afford it so went ahead with the invasive procedure since they said they were comfortable doing it. Unfortunately things didn't go well during surgery and my pet had complications. Another vet who saw her later was pretty concerned about the size of the incision and how it was healing. Staff were kind which I appreciated, but I expected better from a clinic that said they could handle this. Just wanted to share in case it helps someone else.
16+ year client over two cats. Best place for squishing.
$155.00 just for a first consultation. Vvvv expensive

​I brought my bearded dragon here with symptoms I knew were serious, but my concerns were completely dismissed.

The veterinarian I saw showed a severe lack of knowledge regarding reptile emergencies and insisted I simply "come back in a few weeks." Had I followed that advice, my pet would have died.

​During the consultation, the vet's primary focus was questioning my care setup. I was told to spend the next couple of weeks trying to supplement her with vitamins and ensure her husbandry was perfect. I was advised that after this delay, she would either improve, OR her condition would potentially become gravely worse (e.g., developing peritonitis), at which point they would consider surgery.

This suggestion is medically unacceptable and dangerous. It put supportive care ahead of an obvious, life-threatening crisis and risked delaying surgery until she was critically ill, severely reducing her chances of survival.

​I rushed my bearded dragon to Capitol Hill Veterinary Hospital, who specialize in reptiles, and within the 5 minute examination where they check the color of her gums, they use the Doppler to check her heart and they used an ultrasound to check her belly- they immediately recognized her dire, life-threatening condition and booked her in for emergency surgery the following morning!

The diagnosis was pre-ovulatory follicular stasis that required immediate intervention and was never going to resolve spontaneously or with any amount of supportive care.

The reptile specialist also confirmed that my setup was excellent, better than 98% of owners, proving the initial vet was focusing on the wrong problem.

​Adding to the frustration, the vet I saw was rude and unprofessional. Instead of speaking to me in the examination room or even in person, they called my phone while I was sitting in the lobby to communicate.

​Key Takeaways:
•​Veterinarian lacked specialized knowledge for critically ill reptiles.
•​Dismissed serious symptoms and gave dangerous advice regarding surgical timing, prioritizing delayed supportive care over emergency intervention.
•​Poor communication and rude service.
•​Wasted critical time that endangered my pet.

​While I'm sure this clinic is great for dogs, cats, and common small mammals, do not bring your critically ill reptile here. When time is of the essence, their lack of expertise and poor judgment could be fatal.

We brought our rat here last minute as our usual vet clinic had already closed for the day and we thought it was urgent. Dr Uri was condescending and insensitive. He also didn't even address the problem we came in for but rather insisted on performing a surgery then tried to leave the room after less than 5 minutes of looking at our rat. I had to insist on further inspection and insight into what was going on with her. Afterwards, he provided a quote for the surgery, asked us how much our usual vet had quoted us for, and said "oh I should really increase my prices, I'm way better than them".

Staff was awesome, facilities were clean, centrally located, the website was great.

10/10 we will be back.

Thanks to the team at Arbutus West Animal Clinic
When I googled “Granville Island Vet”, it was disappointing to see your business paying for AdWords under your competitor’s name.

The staff here are all great, but I have to say, the lead vet tech (I think his name is NJ) - he is seriously amazing.  He has been involved with my dog Beans on multiple surgeries, and the care and compassion he shows for both animals and their human companions is so reassuring during stressful visits. He is also extremely thorough and knowledgeable, and makes sure to explain everything.

I don't often write reviews but felt I had too. Disappointed with the care my pet received. I was informed about the laparoscopic spay option after being quoted for an invasive spay but couldn’t afford it, so I agreed to the invasive spay they said they could perform (comfortably). Unfortunately, the procedure was poorly done, and my pet had complications during surgery. A vet who later reviewed the large incision and healing process expressed concern. I expected better from a clinic that claimed they were comfortable with this method. I am very thankful for the kind staff but had to write this review so maybe it can be done or avoided next time.

A few days ago, my bearded dragon suddenly became lethargic and developed a black beard. Unfortunately, our usual veterinarian was closed. My daughter reached out and asked if I could take her to see someone. Initially, the staff was a bit hesitant since this was an emergency and they had never seen her before. However, they eventually agreed to see her between appointments. The front staff was incredibly patient, and I must say, the doctor there truly saved my bearded dragon's life. Her heart rate was dangerously low, and she could have died from her unexpected illness. They provided her with medication to help, and if it weren't for the quick thinking and care of the doctor and his staff, I doubt she would have survived. I can't express enough gratitude for their attention to our scaly baby's needs, especially on such short notice. She has returned to her usual self, and you and your team are like angels. Thank you from the depths of our hearts. You are an outstanding team and an impeccable, honest doctor who truly knows his craft. Peach, my daughter, and I are so grateful. I felt reassured when I rushed to the back and lifted her blanket, worried about her condition, and the doctor advised me not to disturb her, saying she needed a warm blanket and to leave her be. I genuinely respect that straightforward approach; doctors who get things done aren’t worried to say what they should especially in an emergency situation ! To all the reviews I’ve read about this doctor’s personality, I can attest that he saved my bearded dragon's life! If he can help, he will! Unfortunately, some things are beyond saving, but I know that if he can, he will! I witnessed it firsthand! This doctor & staff will be seeing Peach again for wellness checks and other needs. We are so delighted that she is doing better. Thank you once again, Doctor and team! 🙌🏻🤌🏻🫰🏻 You all saved her life, which is incredible! 🥰 I've included a photo of her today, looking amazing!

We initially went here with our rescue ball python several years ago & Dr Burstyn was helpful in getting us set up with the ins & outs of ball python care. When we got our new puppy, we wanted to continue to work with this clinic given the positive experience but there was absolutely nothing positive in our few visits with our puppy & we quickly switched to a much more caring and professional vet clinic. At Arbutus 1) we were not allowed to go into the clinic with our puppy, 2) both vets we dealt with were condescending & unhelpful & our puppy would leave extremely anxious & overstimulated (Dr Burstyn yelled that it was my fault my puppy was having digestive problems — which were later diagnosed to be completely unrelated to his assumption*)  3) the final time we brought our puppy there, when the tech brought him out & we were getting ready to leave, the tech leaned over to the front desk assistant, rolling his eyes & said ‘god, I wish we were a cat only clinic’.

* I am open to being educated! In this case, he was incorrect but yelling at a patient’s guardian even if he *had* been correct is completely unprofessional.

At our current clinic that we switched to after the above experiences with Arbutus, they allowed us to stay with our puppy during exams (which helped him stay calm), they enjoy & respect him & earned his trust, & he reciprocates by trying his best to help with whatever procedure they’re doing (it’s so sweet!) They provide thorough education & are up on the latest research, & have shown genuine care & enthusiasm to all the animals (& guardians) who come into the office. It is night & day different from our experience at arbutus.

I went to the arbutus animal clinic when my cat Callie had an eye infection. The first vet I saw there was a really sweet woman, she let me be present during the exam and explains everything to me and answered all my questions. It was a great experience so I decided to go back as my previous vet was a far commute.

However, my experience with Dr. Uri the next time Callie had an eye infection was entirely different. As many of the other reviews mention here, he was extremely condescending. One of my cats was diagnosed with a heart murmur when she was 6 months old. This was confirmed by 2 different vets at the shelter she came from, a 3rd vet when I adopted her, and a 4th who did a cardiac ultrasound for her. Dr. Uri told me she had no murmur, said that most likely the other vets just said she had a murmur because the previous one had (while also making a racist comment about one of the Pakistani vets that saw her), and wrote on her patient history that “Most likely Patient has never had a murmur” and “Treat as not having cardiac disease at this time.”

Recently Lila had to go to the emergency vet where they asked me if I knew she had a murmur (without my prompting!) and said that they’d have to use special “heart safe” anesthesia for her. Dr. Uri’s casualness to dismiss my cats heart murmur could have led to her being given the wrong type of anesthesia down the line.

This type of holier than thou attitude was present throughout all of my visits. He had no willingness to work with me and my cats and only wanted to do things “his way”. During previous exams at her previous vet (and even blood draws!) Callie has been completely calm and cooperative if you give her squeezey treats. I tried to suggest using the treat I brought for her while he was looking at her eyes and she was squirming but he rudely cut me off before I could finish my sentence saying “There’s nothing you can do to help here”. When they took her back for a blood draw I once again offered up the squeezey treat and said “She’s really good with blood draws if you use one of these, you can take it if you want”. He said to me “We’re really good at blood draws so we don’t need it.”. They took Callie to the back and a few minutes later I heard her loudly meowing which she has NEVER done during bloodwork when she’s being given squeezey treats. I then heard him say “The owner says she’s better with a treat”. The visit could’ve been much more comfortable if he’d been willing to work with us.

He also told me to give one of my cat’s L-Lysine and suggested a supplement that they had in the front, looking at it and going “yeah sure that has Lysine in it”. He handed me the he supplement but I looked at the actual amount of lysine it had and it was barely any. I would've had to give my cat nearly the whole bottle every day for her to get the amount of lysine which has been scientifically proven to reduce eye infections.

If you read through other negative reviews you can see the tone with which the clinic responds to them. This is the same tone Dr. Uri used with us most visits. He will tell you he's "one of the best vets in North America" and seems to have an inflated ego due to having a lot of views on YouTube. It doesn't give him the right to talk down to owners who are just trying to understand what's best for their pet. I'd recommend steering clear.

Always made time for my rabbit in emergency situations (GI Stasis). He sadly passed away and they sent a handheld card signed by everyone at the clinic. They care a ton about your pet. Highly recommend
Highly recommended 👏 …

I brought my pet here and received good medical care from the staff, for which I’m grateful. However, I was deeply disturbed by racist comments made by the owner/lead vet.  When I mentioned that my pet would be going to Langley Animal Clinic for surgery, the owner/lead vet stated that Indian and Persian doctors work there, therefore they likely obtained their degrees overseas and were probably unqualified "animal butchers."  This kind of language is completely unacceptable, especially in a profession built on compassion and care. No amount of skill can make up for that kind of blatant prejudice. I cannot, in good conscience, support a business where such views are expressed.
So friendly and caring

The veterinarian’s attitude during my last visit left me dissatisfied. Mocking or dismissing recommendations from other sources felt unnecessary. With so much variation in research, clinics, and breeders, a more positive and respectful approach to sharing advice would have been far more effective than putting others down.

Additionally, many responses to negative reviews seem condescending, offensive, and defensive, which gives the impression that criticism is not welcomed positively. It took me some time to write this, as my past experiences were positive. I hope this review is taken as a constructive opportunity to improve rather than as something hurtful.

This animal clinic is a real gem. Starting with Dr Burstyn, a passionate animal advocate, I am really grateful for his ethical practice and kind heart. He provided complete and clear diagnosis about my cat’s condition and professional …
Feel like it was better a few years ago. I feel kinda detached from the medical staff now... Seems not so easy to go back with him (our dog) and not fully comfortable with their diagnoses
Friendly and very professional. Great service. Highly recommended
Terrible vet for reptiles. Ignored the early stages of a disease that killed my gecko. Told me I was making up symptoms and refused to help further. …

Reptile care at this clinic is terrible!! For dogs, cats and rabbits they have great reviews, but they do not know how to handle reptiles. Beware that your reptile could be injured by improper techniques and handling. Unfortunately …
